title: Exhaustion gate (r1 W3 fix) compares two incompatible timestamp formats lexically — correct only under a UTC session and an incidental 'T' > ' ' byte ordering
evidence: find_reference_call_by_send_ref.sql: `SELECT e->>'at' FROM jsonb_array_elements(rc.attempts) AS e WHERE e->>'detail' = $4 AND e->>'outcome' = 'delivered' ORDER BY e->>'at' DESC LIMIT 1` AS matched_send_at; `COALESCE(rc.corrected_at::text, '') AS corrected_at`. webhooks.gleam:304: `// ISO timestamps — lexical compare is chronological. string.compare(at, corrected) != order.Lt`. sweep.gleam:180 writes attempts `at` via `timestamp.to_rfc3339(calendar.utc_offset)` ('T'/'Z' form), while `corrected_at::text` is Postgres's space-separated, session-TimeZone-dependent rendering ('YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.ffffff+00').
detail: The comment's premise is false: the two strings share no format. Under a non-UTC session (e.g. Europe/Dublin), the local-date shift at the day boundary misclassifies both directions: a stale pre-correction bounce can be judged genuine (re-fabricating referee_contact_invalid — the r1 W3 defect) and a genuine post-correction failure judged stale (row never exhausts, nudge loop forever). Tests pass because their hardcoded dates are >10 days apart.
recommended_fix: Compare in SQL as timestamptz: gate on `(SELECT e->>'at' ...)::timestamptz >= rc.corrected_at` (or to_char both with one fixed format), so the gate is format- and timezone-proof.

title: STILL PRESENT (r1): spec Files list names update_application_referee_trio.sql which does not exist and miscounts new vs edited SQL
evidence: Line 189 NEW list: `server/src/reference_checks/sql/update_application_referee_trio.sql` — on disk the trio updates are three files (update_application_referee_trio_landlord/_character/_employer.sql). The EDIT list omits sweep_advance.sql / sweep_claim_t0.sql / sweep_due_reference_calls.sql (all edited) and the NEW list omits exhaust_reference_call.sql / rearm_queued_reference_calls.sql / verify_application_in_vacancy.sql (all added).
detail: The rework added a 'Perkins r1 rework' section but left the Files section stale: one phantom filename and the SQL edit/new accounting still wrong, so the spec cannot serve as the change manifest.

title: STILL PRESENT (r1): substitute_reference_call.sql duplicates the live-slot ON CONFLICT predicate instead of reusing the existing idempotent insert
evidence: substitute_reference_call.sql:37-46: `ON CONFLICT (application_id, ref_slot, owner_label) WHERE status NOT IN ('form_completed', 'unreachable', 'refused', 'objected', 'manual_recorded', 'failed', 'completed', 'partial') DO NOTHING` — the same predicate is now maintained in three places: idx_reference_call_live (20260731222000_create_reference_call.sql:138-140), insert_reference_call_if_absent.sql, and here.
detail: Postgres infers the arbiter index from this predicate; any drift in the status list between the index and either statement breaks ON CONFLICT inference at runtime (500 on substitute/start). The r1 note was not folded.
recommended_fix: Extract the live-slot status list into one shared constant (Squirrel cannot parameterize it, but a single comment-anchored canonical copy plus a schema test comparing the three texts keeps them pinned).
